# Renderer SDK API

The public API of the renderer SDK: `@githubnext/projections/renderer` (the frame protocol client, presentation
helpers, interactions, rings and languages), `@githubnext/projections/renderer/react` (the React hooks) and
`@githubnext/projections/vite` (the build), by the SDK module that defines each export. Read with the `typescript-public-api` extractor, the same one that shows your own packages'
APIs; descriptions are the sources' documentation comments. Start with [the renderer SDK guide](../../packages/renderers/sdk/README.md).

## Client (`@githubnext/projections/renderer`)

### `afterPaint`

```ts
afterPaint(callback: { (): void }, view?: Window, fallbackMs?: number): { (): void }
```

Calls `callback` once after the browser has painted the current frame.
Browsers pause animation frames in hidden or offscreen cross-origin frames,
where nothing is painted; a short timer then acknowledges instead.

### `applyEnvironment`

```ts
applyEnvironment(environment: RendererEnvironment, element?: HTMLElement): void
```

Exposes the host theme to CSS as `--projections-<token>` custom properties,
sets `color-scheme`, marks reduced motion with `data-reduced-motion="true"`
and a held pane of side by side or swipe with `data-pane="before|after"` on
the element (the document element by default).

### `ConnectOptions`

```ts
interface ConnectOptions
```

What `connectRenderer` declares, and where it connects.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `capabilities` | `"capabilities": RendererCapabilities` | What the renderer supports, posted in `ready`; the host sends optional messages only for declared capabilities. Invalid `controls` make `connectRenderer` throw. |
| `rings` | `"rings"?: false` | Hover, focus and selection rings on every entity's unit, as styling on the unit's own element (see `connectRings`). On by default; `false` leaves them to the renderer, which the renderer checks then hold to the same contract. |
| `window` | `"window"?: Window` | Defaults to the global window. Supplied in tests. |

### `connectRenderer`

```ts
connectRenderer(handlers: RendererHandlers, options: ConnectOptions): RendererClient
```

Connects a renderer document to its host. Reads the channel nonce and host
origin from the URL fragment, starts listening, and posts `ready` with the
renderer's capabilities. Messages that do not come from the parent window,
carry another channel or fail validation are ignored. When a document connects again on the same channel (a
development server's hot update), the host's current state is replayed to the new handlers.

### `EmbeddedRenderer`

```ts
interface EmbeddedRenderer
```

A nested renderer frame, from `embedRenderer`: what to send it, and how to stop it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dispose` | `"dispose"(): void` | Stops listening and removes the frame. |
| `hover` | `"hover"(id: null \| string): void` | Sent only when the nested renderer declares `hover`. |
| `iframe` | `readonly "iframe": HTMLIFrameElement` | The sandboxed frame, transparent until the nested renderer has painted. |
| `ready` | `readonly "ready": Promise<RendererCapabilities>` | Resolves with the nested renderer's capabilities once it is ready; rejects when it fails. |
| `select` | `"select"(id: null \| string): void` | Selects an item, by the nested renderer's own selection ID, or clears the selection (`null`). |
| `setEnvironment` | `"setEnvironment"(environment: RendererEnvironment): void` | Sends a new theme, motion preference, locale or pane; `sizing` stays `fill` unless it says otherwise. |
| `setInit` | `"setInit"(init: RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } \| RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" }, progress?: ProgressPayload \| undefined): void` | Replaces what it presents (a new `init`), and optionally the position. |
| `setOptions` | `"setOptions"(options: RendererOptions): void` | Replaces its settings. |
| `setProgress` | `"setProgress"(progress: ProgressPayload): void` | Sends a new position to draw. |

### `EmbedOptions`

```ts
interface EmbedOptions
```

What `embedRenderer` runs and how it reports back.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `colorMode` | `"colorMode"?: "dark" \| "light"` | The color mode its document paints before `init`, so its first paint matches; default `init`'s, else light. |
| `init` | `"init": RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } \| RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" } \| { (capabilities: RendererCapabilities): RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } \| RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" } }` | What the nested renderer presents, and its environment; `sizing` defaults to `fill`, the frame's own size. A function is called with the renderer's capabilities once it is ready, to choose for them (diff or animated). |
| `onFailure` | `"onFailure"?: { (message: string): void }` | Called once when the frame can't run: the host refused its document, or it never became ready. |
| `onMessage` | `"onMessage"?: { (message: { "capabilities": RendererCapabilities; "type": "ready" } \| { "controls": Array<{ "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": false \| true; "type": "toggle" } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "icon"?: "collapse" \| "download" \| "expand" \| "filter" \| "fit" \| "next" \| "previous" \| "reset" \| "search" \| "settings" \| "zoom-in" \| "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>; "type": "controls" } \| { "ends": Array<number>; "slots"?: number; "type": "steps" } \| { "id": null \| string; "path"?: string; "type": "select" } \| { "id": null \| string; "type": "hover" } \| { "id": string; "rect": AnchorRect \| null; "type": "anchor" } \| { "id": string; "type": "annotation" } \| { "id": string; "type": "control"; "value": false \| number \| string \| true } \| { "line"?: number; "path": string; "type": "open" } \| { "message": string; "type": "error" } \| { "progress": number; "type": "rendered" } \| { "px": number; "type": "height" } \| { "ratio": number; "type": "aspect" } \| { "renderer": string; "type": "document-request" } \| { "type": "legend" } & RendererLegend \| { "type": "summary" } & RendererSummary \| { "type": "viewport" } & ScrollPosition): void }` | Each valid message the nested renderer sends, after `embedRenderer` has handled it (`ready`, `rendered`, `height` and nested `document-request`s are handled; a host can follow `select`, `hover`, `error` and the rest). |
| `options` | `"options"?: RendererOptions` | Its settings, as `options` would carry them. |
| `progress` | `"progress"?: ProgressPayload \| { (capabilities: RendererCapabilities): ProgressPayload \| undefined }` | The position to draw, or a function of the capabilities; omitted, its opening state (an extraction, or a diff). |
| `renderer` | `"renderer": string` | The built-in renderer to run, by name, for example `graph`. |
| `title` | `"title": string` | The frame's accessible name, for example `Service platform, drawn by the graph renderer`. |

### `embedRenderer`

```ts
embedRenderer(client: Pick<RendererClient, "requestDocument">, container: HTMLElement, options: EmbedOptions): EmbeddedRenderer
```

Runs the built-in renderer `options.renderer` in a sandboxed frame appended to `container`, acting as its host. The
document comes from this renderer's host (`client.requestDocument`), which supplies only built-in renderers; the
frame is `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc>`, so it inherits this document's content security policy and gets
an opaque origin of its own. Messages are accepted only from that frame, on its own channel, and only if they
validate strictly. The frame fills `container` and stays transparent until its renderer has painted.

### `RendererClient`

```ts
interface RendererClient
```

A renderer's side of the conversation with its host, from `connectRenderer`. Each method posts one message; nothing
is posted after `dispose`. IDs and error messages are truncated to `rendererLimits.textLength`, and coordinates
are rounded to hundredths of a pixel.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `anchor` | `"anchor"(id: string, rect: AnchorRect \| null): void` | Reports where an entity is drawn, in this document's viewport, or `null` when it isn't visible (capability `anchors`). |
| `annotation` | `"annotation"(id: string): void` | Reports that the person activated the annotation marker on an item (capability `annotations`); call `select(id)` first. |
| `aspect` | `"aspect"(ratio: number): void` | Reports the shape (width / height) of the content the renderer fits to its stage, over the whole transition, so a host can arrange held panes for the larger fitted scale. Clamped to `rendererLimits.aspect`. |
| `channel` | `readonly "channel": string` | The frame's channel nonce, from the URL fragment. |
| `declareOptions` | `"declareOptions"(controls: Array<{ "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": false \| true; "type": "toggle" } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "icon"?: "collapse" \| "download" \| "expand" \| "filter" \| "fit" \| "next" \| "previous" \| "reset" \| "search" \| "settings" \| "zoom-in" \| "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>): void` | Replaces the controls the host draws for this renderer (initially those in `capabilities.controls`). Throws if a declaration is invalid. |
| `dispose` | `"dispose"(): void` | Stops listening for host messages. |
| `error` | `"error"(message: string): void` | Reports a rendering failure. The host shows it and keeps its own views available. |
| `height` | `"height"(px: number): void` | Requests a frame height in CSS pixels. The host clamps it. |
| `hover` | `"hover"(id: null \| string): void` | Reports the entity under the pointer (capability `hover`). |
| `legend` | `"legend"(legend: RendererLegend): void` | Asks the host to draw the renderer's legend once beside the frames, with the host's design system, instead of drawing one in each pane. Items use theme tokens (preferred) or CSS colors; an empty list clears it. Throws when the legend is invalid. |
| `observeHeight` | `"observeHeight"(element: Element): { (): void }` | Requests the height of `element` whenever it resizes. Returns a function that stops observing. |
| `open` | `"open"(path: string, line?: number \| undefined): void` | Asks the host to open a repository file; the host decides whether to navigate. |
| `rendered` | `"rendered"(progress: number): void` | Acknowledges that the frame for `progress` has been painted. |
| `requestDocument` | `"requestDocument"(name: string): Promise<string>` | Asks the host for the document of the built-in renderer `name` (for example `graph`), to run in a frame nested in this one (`embedRenderer` does both). Resolves with its `index.html` text, as the host runs it; rejects with the host's reason when it supplies none (an unknown or custom renderer, or a host without documents), or after `rendererLimits.documentTimeoutMs` without an answer. Repeated requests for one name share one answer. |
| `select` | `"select"(id: null \| string, path?: string \| undefined): void` | Reports the renderer's selection, or `null` when it clears it. `path`, an RFC 6901 pointer such as `/data/owner`, selects a property of the item (capability `properties`); it is ignored with a `null` ID and throws if invalid. |
| `setControl` | `"setControl"(id: string, value: false \| number \| string \| true): void` | Sets a declared control's value from the renderer's own content, as the person changed it there (a sortable column header, say). The host applies it as if they had set it in its settings and answers with `options`; it ignores a value the control doesn't accept. |
| `steps` | `"steps"(ends: Array<number>, slots?: number \| undefined): void` | Declares progress values at which the host may hold during playback, and optionally how many step slots the presentation spans (`timelineSlots`), for the host's default pace. |
| `subscribe` | `"subscribe"(listener: { (message: { "height": number; "type": "viewport"; "width": number } \| { "id": null \| string; "path"?: string; "type": "select" } \| { "id": null \| string; "type": "hover" } \| { "id": string; "type": "action" } \| { "items": Array<AnnotationMark>; "type": "annotations" } \| { "options": RendererOptions; "type": "options" } \| { "type": "document" } & { "renderer": string } & { "error": string; "html"?: never } \| { "type": "document" } & { "renderer": string } & { "error"?: never; "html": string } \| { "type": "environment" } & RendererEnvironment \| { "type": "filter" } & FilterPayload \| { "type": "init" } & RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } \| { "type": "init" } & RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" } \| { "type": "progress" } & ProgressPayload \| { "type": "scroll" } & ScrollPosition): void }): { (): void }` | Observes every valid host message after the handlers run. Returns a function that stops observing. |
| `summary` | `"summary"(summary: RendererSummary): void` | Gives the host the words for its summary bar: a figure per extraction kind in the renderer's vocabulary (`SummaryItem`), in display order; an empty list returns the bar to the host's own words. Throws when the summary is invalid. |
| `viewport` | `"viewport"(position: ScrollPosition): void` | Reports that the person scrolled a container (capability `scrollSync`). |

### `RendererConnectionError`

```ts
class RendererConnectionError extends Error
```

Thrown when a renderer can't connect or is asked to send something invalid: outside a host frame, without a channel
in the URL fragment, or with invalid controls, legend, summary or selection path.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `captureStackTrace` | `static "captureStackTrace"(targetObject: object, constructorOpt?: Function \| undefined): void` |  |
| `cause` | `"cause"?: unknown` |  |
| `constructor` | `new (message: string): RendererConnectionError` |  |
| `message` | `"message": string` |  |
| `name` | `"name": string` |  |
| `prepareStackTrace` | `static "prepareStackTrace"(err: Error, stackTraces: Array<CallSite>): any` |  |
| `stack` | `"stack"?: string` |  |
| `stackTraceLimit` | `static "stackTraceLimit": number` |  |

### `RendererHandlers`

```ts
interface RendererHandlers
```

Handlers for host messages. Each is optional; unknown or foreign messages never reach them.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | `"action"?(message: { id: string; }): void` | The person activated one of the renderer's `action` controls. |
| `annotations` | `"annotations"?(items: Array<AnnotationMark>): void` | Markers to draw on items, replacing earlier ones (capability `annotations`). |
| `environment` | `"environment"?(message: RendererEnvironment): void` | A new theme, motion preference, locale, pane or sizing; `applyEnvironment` applies it to CSS. |
| `filter` | `"filter"?(message: { scope?: string[] \| null; ids: string[] \| null; query: string; changesOnly: boolean; }): void` | The host's find and "changes only" settings changed. |
| `hover` | `"hover"?(message: { id: string \| null; }): void` | The entity the person points at in any pane, or `null` (capability `hover`). |
| `init` | `"init"?(message: RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } \| RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" }): void` | The document to present and the environment, first after `ready` and again whenever the host replaces the document; reset any per-document state. |
| `options` | `"options"?(options: RendererOptions): void` | New settings, replacing the earlier ones: declared controls' values by `id` (see `controlValues`). |
| `progress` | `"progress"?(message: ProgressPayload): void` | A new position to draw; acknowledge it with `client.rendered` once painted. |
| `scroll` | `"scroll"?(position: ScrollPosition): void` | Scroll a container to mirror another pane (capability `scrollSync`); don't report that scroll as `viewport`. |
| `select` | `"select"?(message: { path?: string; id: string \| null; }): void` | The host's selection: an item ID or `null`, and optionally a property of it (`path`, an RFC 6901 pointer). |
| `viewport` | `"viewport"?(message: { height: number; width: number; }): void` | The frame's size in CSS px, on load and whenever it changes. |

## Interactions (`@githubnext/projections/renderer`)

### `annotatedAttribute`

```ts
annotatedAttribute: "data-projections-annotated"
```

Attribute the controller sets on every entity element the host has annotated (`annotations`).

### `AnnotationAnchor`

```ts
type AnnotationAnchor = "bottom-left" | "bottom-right" | "top-left" | "top-right"
```

One of `annotationAnchors`.

### `annotationAnchorAttribute`

```ts
annotationAnchorAttribute: "data-projections-annotation-anchor"
```

Attribute a renderer may set on an item (or an ancestor) to choose the corner its annotation badge straddles:
`top-left` (default), `top-right`, `bottom-left` or `bottom-right`.

### `annotationAnchors`

```ts
annotationAnchors: readonly ["top-left", "top-right", "bottom-left", "bottom-right"]
```

The corners an annotation badge can straddle, the values of `annotationAnchorAttribute`.

### `annotationAttribute`

```ts
annotationAttribute: "data-projections-annotation"
```

Attribute that carries the annotated item's selection ID on each annotation badge.

### `annotationName`

```ts
annotationName(mark: AnnotationMark, item?: string | undefined): string
```

The accessible name of an annotation badge: the mark's label, or its count,
on the item's accessible name (or its ID when it has none).

### `connectInteractions`

```ts
connectInteractions(client: RendererClient, root: HTMLElement, options?: InteractionOptions): InteractionController
```

Implements hover, anchors, scroll mirroring, the host's filter and
annotation badges for any renderer whose entities carry their selection ID
in `data-entity-id` (or `attribute`):

- Pointer and focus on an entity report `hover`; the host's `hover` marks
  every element of that entity with `data-projections-hovered`, which the
  renderer styles.
- The selected and hovered entities' visible rectangles are reported as
  `anchor` messages after every scroll, resize or DOM change.
- Scrolling a container reports `viewport`; the host's `scroll` scrolls the
  matching container without echoing it back.
- A selection that arrives from the host (chosen in another pane or view)
  scrolls the item into view if a scrolling container hides it, without
  mirroring that scroll to the other pane, and briefly pulses its elements
  (`data-projections-pulse`, never under reduced motion), so the counterpart
  of a selection is in view and easy to find.
- The host's `annotations` mark annotated entity elements with
  `data-projections-annotated` and draw a badge button on each visible one,
  in an overlay outside `root`. Activating a badge selects the item and
  reports `annotation`. Visible annotated items' anchors are reported too,
  at a bounded rate.

### `filteredAttribute`

```ts
filteredAttribute: "data-projections-filtered"
```

Attribute the controller sets on every entity element the host's filter excludes.

### `hoveredAttribute`

```ts
hoveredAttribute: "data-projections-hovered"
```

Attribute the controller sets on every element of the entity the host says is hovered.

### `interactionCapabilities`

```ts
interactionCapabilities: { "anchors": true; "annotations": true; "filter": true; "hover": true; "scrollSync": true }
```

Capabilities a renderer using `connectInteractions` can declare.

### `InteractionController`

```ts
interface InteractionController
```

The running interactions of one root (`connectInteractions`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dispose` | `"dispose"(): void` | Stops listening and observing, removes badges and annotation marks, and releases the document's rings. |
| `refresh` | `"refresh"(): void` | Re-measures anchors and badges, for layout changes the controller can't observe. |
| `selection` | `readonly "selection": { "id": null \| string; "path"?: string }` | The latest selection, from `setSelected`, the host's `select` (with its property `path`) or an annotation badge. |
| `setSelected` | `"setSelected"(id: null \| string): void` | The renderer's current selection, whose position is reported as an anchor. |

### `InteractionOptions`

```ts
interface InteractionOptions
```

How `connectInteractions` finds entities and reports badge selections.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `attribute` | `"attribute"?: string` | Attribute that carries an element's selection ID (default `data-entity-id`). |
| `select` | `"select"?: { (id: string): void }` | Reports a selection when the person activates an annotation badge, in place of `client.select`, so the renderer can update its own selection too. It must still call `client.select(id)`. |
| `window` | `"window"?: Window` | Defaults to the root's window. |

### `pulseAttribute`

```ts
pulseAttribute: "data-projections-pulse"
```

Marks an item selected elsewhere while it pulses.

### `scrollAttribute`

```ts
scrollAttribute: "data-projections-scroll"
```

Attribute that names a scroll container for mirroring between panes.

### `unitAttribute`

```ts
unitAttribute: "data-projections-unit"
```

Marks the entity element that is one visual unit (a card, a table) when
entity elements nest inside it. The SDK rings units (see `rings.ts`);
nested parts are tinted by the renderer, never ringed.

## Languages (`@githubnext/projections/renderer`)

### `Language`

```ts
interface Language
```

Programming languages and file types as GitHub Linguist names them, with
Linguist's language colors, so a language looks the same in every renderer
and as it does on github.com. The table is generated from Linguist's
`languages.yml` at a pinned release (`linguistRelease`; MIT, its notice
travels with every bundle that includes it). Programming and markup
languages have a color, adjusted per theme only as much as it takes to
reach 3:1 against the stage background and to stay apart from more common
languages; data and prose (JSON, YAML, Markdown) have none, so renderers
give them categorical colors.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | `"color"?: { "dark": string; "light": string; "linguist": string }` | Linguist's own color, for programming and markup languages. |
| `group` | `"group": string` | The language a variant is presented as (TSX is TypeScript); its own name otherwise. |
| `name` | `"name": string` | Linguist's name, for example `TypeScript`. |
| `type` | `"type": "data" \| "markup" \| "programming" \| "prose"` | Linguist's category: `programming` and `markup` languages have a `color`; `data` and `prose` don't. |

### `languageColor`

```ts
languageColor(language: Language, colorMode: "dark" | "light"): string | undefined
```

A language's color for a theme: the color of its group (TSX is drawn as
TypeScript), or `undefined` for data and prose and for languages Linguist
gives no color.

### `languageNamed`

```ts
languageNamed(name: string): Language | undefined
```

The language a name or alias denotes (`TypeScript`, `ts`, `bash`, `C Header`), ignoring case.

### `languageOfPath`

```ts
languageOfPath(path: string): Language | undefined
```

The language of a repository path: by its file name (`Dockerfile`,
`Makefile`), else by its longest known extension (`.d.ts` before `.ts`).

### `linguistRelease`

```ts
linguistRelease: string
```

The Linguist release the language table was generated from, for example `v9.7.0`.

## Presentation (`@githubnext/projections/renderer`)

### `adjectivalKind`

```ts
adjectivalKind(words: Array<string>): false | true
```

Whether a kind's words read as an adjective (`hidden`, `deprecated`, `not patchable`), which English counts without a plural.

### `BasisValue`

```ts
type BasisValue = Readonly<Record<string, string>>
```

A basis value as the extraction records it: named parts.

### `changeContext`

```ts
changeContext(rows: Array<ScopeRow>, revisions: { "after": ContainmentSource; "before": ContainmentSource }, changes?: Iterable<string, any, any> | undefined): ChangesScope
```

The context of a comparison's changes: each change's own (`Change.context`, the Engine's core context and what
comparator rules added), else, for a comparison saved without it, the same structural derivation (`rowContexts`).
Whatever is shown brings what a renderer needs to place it: a relationship its endpoints, and an entity the items
containing it, traversed once for all of them. Context is only ever added, and never hides a change. `changes`
narrows the changes to those row IDs (for example a find or summary filter's); by default every change
(`isScopeChange`) is in scope.

### `ChangesScope`

```ts
interface ChangesScope
```

What a Changes scope shows: the changes it is about and the unchanged items that give them context.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `changes` | `"changes": ReadonlySet<string>` | The change rows in scope, by row ID. |
| `context` | `"context": ReadonlySet<string>` | The unchanged rows shown to read them: their relationships' endpoints and the items that contain them. |
| `shown` | `"shown": ReadonlySet<string>` | Both: every row the scope shows. |

### `CodeStatisticsMeasure`

```ts
type CodeStatisticsMeasure = "blank" | "code" | "comment" | "files" | "lines"
```

Which code-statistics count to show: lines of code, comment lines, blank lines, all lines or files.

### `codeStatisticsMeasures`

```ts
codeStatisticsMeasures: Array<{ "id": "blank" | "code" | "comment" | "files" | "lines"; "label": string; "unit": string }>
```

Every measure with its display label and the unit its rows carry, in menu order.

### `CodeStatisticsOptions`

```ts
interface CodeStatisticsOptions
```

How a code-statistics view measures and charts its counts (`ViewerState.statistics`, `statisticsRows`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `byLanguage` | `"byLanguage": false \| true` | One row per language, or `false` for the whole repository's code, comment and blank lines. |
| `chart` | `"chart": "bars" \| "share" \| "table"` | `bars` for absolute values, `share` for each row's share of the total (`quantityShares`), `table` for every count in a sortable table. |
| `measure` | `"measure": "blank" \| "code" \| "comment" \| "files" \| "lines"` | The count each language row shows; ignored without `byLanguage`, which always shows code, comments and blanks. |
| `scope` | `"scope": "all" \| "other" \| "tests"` | Which files the counts cover. |

### `CodeStatisticsScope`

```ts
type CodeStatisticsScope = "all" | "other" | "tests"
```

Which files a count covers: every file, files the extractor classified as tests, or the rest.

### `codeStatisticsScopes`

```ts
codeStatisticsScopes: Array<{ "id": "all" | "other" | "tests"; "label": string }>
```

Every scope with its display label, in menu order.

### `compileTimeline`

```ts
compileTimeline<T>(steps: Array<T>, options?: { "lead"?: { (step: T): false | true }; "tail"?: { (step: T): false | true } }): Array<T & { "hold": number; "lead": number; "radius": number; "tail": number; "time": number }>
```

Turns ordered steps into windows on [0, 1], separated by holds. Comparisons
carry order and grouping only; this presentation timing is the renderer's.
Each step's slot is `gap` wide: its motion window takes `1 - stepHoldShare`
of the slot and the rest is a hold shared with its neighbour, so no step
begins before the previous one has finished and settled. A step `lead`
accepts gets a reading lead of `readingShare` slots before its motion, and
one `tail` accepts a reading tail as long after it. Positions depend only
on the sequence and are centred on the midpoint, so reversing a sequence
mirrors its timeline exactly.

### `ContainmentSource`

```ts
type ContainmentSource = { entities: Entity[]; relationships: Relationship[]; schema: "graph/v0" | "dag/v0" | "treemap/v0" | "metrics/v0" | "api/v0" | "database/v0" | "architecture/v0"; vocabularies?: ("dependency-injection/v0" | "infrastructure/v0" | "runtime-policy/v0" | "agentic-workflows/v0" | "scenarios/v0")[]; }
```

The parts of an extraction `isContainment` reads.

### `createFrame`

```ts
createFrame(after: Extraction, changes?: PresentedChanges | undefined, progress?: number, options?: FrameOptions): PresentationFrame
```

Present comparator results at `progress`, following the comparison's steps:
every entity and relationship fades, switches version and crossfades a
rewiring only inside its own step's window (`scheduleSteps`, with the
shared hold policy between steps), so a custom comparator's order is what
plays and shapes settle between steps while progress keeps moving. Pairs
built by hand, without steps, change together in one step. Relationships
never outlive their endpoints. Never infers identity or computes semantic
changes. Report `stepEnds(frame.schedule, direction)` to the host.

### `defaultCodeStatisticsOptions`

```ts
defaultCodeStatisticsOptions: Readonly<CodeStatisticsOptions>
```

Lines of code per language, as bars, over all files.

### `diffEmphasis`

```ts
diffEmphasis(progress: number): number
```

The change emphasis hosts send as `highlighting` while a comparison plays: exactly 0 at both endpoints, easing up
over the first 10% of progress, 1 through the middle, and easing down over the last 10%, so endpoints show each
revision plainly. Progress is clamped to 0 to 1.

### `DirectionLatch`

```ts
class DirectionLatch
```

Chooses which schedule a renderer presents. Under `mirror` order there is
only one. Under `explicit` order the schedule latches to the direction of
travel when progress leaves an endpoint and keeps it until progress reaches
an endpoint again, so reversing mid-transition never jumps to another
timeline. Keep one latch per document.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `constructor` | `new (): DirectionLatch` |  |
| `update` | `"update"(progress: number, direction: -1 \| 1): -1 \| 1` | The direction to present at `progress`, given the current playback `direction`: `1` at progress 0 or below, `-1` at 1 or above, and in between the direction latched when progress left an endpoint (`direction` if it hasn't). |

### `emphasisRise`

```ts
emphasisRise(step: Pick<ScheduledStep, "radius" | "time"> & Partial<Pick<ScheduledStep, "lead" | "tail" | "travel">> | undefined, progress: number): number
```

How much of the host's change highlighting a change in `step` shows at
`progress`: 0 until the step's window begins in the direction the schedule
is travelled (`travel`), then rising (over the first fifth of the reading
part travel enters, else over the start of the motion) to 1, where it stays
until the host's own endpoint fade. Earlier steps never pre-tint later
changes, and an explicit reverse order mirrors it. A change no step places
shows the host's highlighting unscaled.

### `EntityChange`

```ts
interface EntityChange<T>
```

One entity or relationship as presented: its before and after items paired
by the comparison. This is presentation state, not a protocol document.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after"?: T` | The item in the `after` extraction; absent for a removal and a further merged part. |
| `before` | `"before"?: T` | The item in the `before` extraction; absent for an addition and a further split part. |
| `context` | `"context"?: ChangeContext` | The comparison's `change.context`: the other items, by ID in each revision, a person needs to read the change. Absent for unchanged items and in a comparison saved without it; `changeContext` derives it from the structure then. |
| `correspondence` | `"correspondence"?: "declared" \| "exact" \| "merge" \| "none" \| "split"` | How the comparison matched `before` to `after`; absent in a snapshot (`snapshotChanges`). |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The row's stable ID: the comparison change's ID, or the item's own ID for an item the comparison doesn't mention and for the further parts of a split or merge (suffixed `~1`, `~2`… only if that collides). |
| `previousId` | `"previousId"?: string` | The `before` item's ID when `renamed`, for showing what it was called. |
| `renamed` | `"renamed"?: false \| true` | True when the item kept its identity under another ID (a `declared`, `split` or `merge` correspondence). |
| `status` | `"status": "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "unchanged"` | The comparison's status for the item; `unchanged` for items it doesn't mention and in a snapshot. |
| `varied` | `"varied"?: Array<Varied>` | The comparison's `change.varied`: volatile values that differ between the two sides, each within its tolerance or beyond it. An `unchanged` row with `varied` varied only within tolerance and is presented as unchanged; a `modified` one with a value beyond tolerance carries the volatile marker (`variedBeyond`). |

### `entityLabels`

```ts
entityLabels(...extractions: Array<Pick<Extraction, "entities"> | undefined>): { (id: string): string | undefined }
```

Looks up entity labels in extractions, the first that has the entity winning (for example after, then before).

### `entityQuantity`

```ts
entityQuantity(entity: Entity | undefined, key?: string, unit?: string | undefined): Quantity
```

The quantity an entity records in `data[key]` (default `value`), in `unit` or else its `data.unit`. The value is
`undefined` when the entity is absent, the field isn't a finite number, or the entity sets `data.defined` to `false`.

### `filterFrame`

```ts
filterFrame(frame: PresentationFrame, state: Pick<ViewerState, "kind" | "search" | "status">): PresentationFrame
```

`frame` narrowed to the rows `matchesFilter` keeps. A matching relationship brings its endpoints along, so it is
never drawn dangling; a relationship that doesn't match stays when both its endpoints are kept. Other fields are
unchanged.

### `FrameOptions`

```ts
interface FrameOptions
```

How `createFrame` times a comparison.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `"direction"?: -1 \| 1` | The direction of travel this transition presents, from a `DirectionLatch` (default 1). It matters only for a comparison with explicit `reverseSteps`. |
| `schedule` | `"schedule"?: Array<ScheduledStep>` | A schedule to time the frame by; defaults to `scheduleSteps(changes, direction)`. |

### `generatedLabel`

```ts
generatedLabel: "Generated"
```

The accessible name and visible word of the mark every generated field carries.

### `GeneratedPath`

```ts
interface GeneratedPath
```

One generated value of an item: its concrete pointer, and its basis's.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `basis` | `"basis": string` | The pointer to the basis it was generated from, with the same wildcards bound. |
| `path` | `"path": string` | The generated value's RFC 6901 pointer into the item, under `/data/`, with wildcards bound. |

### `generatedPaths`

```ts
generatedPaths(extraction: { readonly "volatile"?: Array<{ "basis"?: string; "collection"?: string; "generated"?: false | true; "kinds"?: Array<string>; "path": string }> | undefined }, item: undefined | { readonly "kind"?: string; readonly [key: string]: unknown }, collection?: "entities" | "relationships"): Array<GeneratedPath>
```

An item's generated values, from the extraction's `volatile` declarations: each concrete pointer (under `/data/`)
a generated declaration matches, with the pointer of its basis. Hosts and renderers mark these fields Generated.

### `generatedText`

```ts
generatedText(value: unknown): string
```

A generated value as text: a string as it is, anything else as indented JSON.

### `generatedTitle`

```ts
generatedTitle: "Generated by the extractor (for example by a language model), not extracted from the code"
```

What the mark means, for its title.

### `generatedWords`

```ts
generatedWords(entry: Pick<Varied, "because" | "reason" | "within">, bases?: undefined | { "after"?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; "before"?: Readonly<Record<string, string>> }): string
```

Why a generated value differs, as protocol prose (code in backtick spans; render it with the kit's `Prose`):
"Regenerated from the same inputs" when the bases are equal, "Regenerated because the input and the prompt
changed" when parts moved (a verbatim part, such as a model ID, with its old and new values), "Generated only
after" for a value on one side only. With the bases, a moved model reads "the model (`a@1` → `a@2`)".

### `genericMetrics`

```ts
genericMetrics(entities: Iterable<Entity | undefined, any, any>): false | true
```

Whether these entities are generic measurements: some carry a numeric `data.value`, and none counts lines or files.

### `hasCodeCounts`

```ts
hasCodeCounts(entities: Iterable<Entity | undefined, any, any>): false | true
```

Whether any of these entities carries line or file counts (`data.code`, `lines` or `files`), as the
code-statistics extractor writes them. Without any, a `metrics/v0` extraction is a set of generic measurements:
each entity's `data.value`, in its `data.unit`.

### `hasTestCounts`

```ts
hasTestCounts(entities: Iterable<Entity | undefined, any, any>): false | true
```

Whether any of these entities carries test counts, so a test/non-test split is meaningful.

### `humanizeKind`

```ts
humanizeKind(kind: string): SummaryNoun
```

The host's word for an extraction kind, when the renderer gives none: its words (`target-framework` → `target
framework`), with a simple English plural (`workspace` → `workspaces`, `policy` → `policies`). A kind already in the
plural keeps it and is made singular (`dependencies` → `dependency`, `imports` → `import`); a kind ending in a
preposition reads the same in both (`applies to`), and so does an adjective (`24 hidden`, `5 not patchable`, `3
deprecated`; see `adjectivalKind`); `depends-on` is a dependency. Common prefixes stay hyphenated (`pre-release` →
`pre-releases`).

### `identifier`

```ts
identifier: { "data-projections-identifier": "" }
```

Spread onto an element (HTML or SVG) to mark it as an identifier: `<span {...identifier}>`.

### `identifierAttribute`

```ts
identifierAttribute: "data-projections-identifier"
```

Marks an element whose text is a code identifier or symbol (a function,
type or package name, a path, route, event name, resource address or ID),
which renderers draw in the theme's monospace font
(`--projections-font-family-mono`) while human-language labels stay in the
sans font. The built-in `identifiers` check verifies that every marked
element computes a monospace font.

### `initialViewerState`

```ts
initialViewerState(progress?: number): ViewerState
```

The state a viewer starts in: no search or filters, the domain view, paused at `progress` (default 1, the after
side) moving forward, nothing selected or collapsed, and `defaultCodeStatisticsOptions`.

### `interpolatedNumber`

```ts
interpolatedNumber(change: EntityChange<Entity>, key: string, progress: number): number | undefined
```

The numeric `data[key]` of an entity at `progress`: linear from the `before` value (at 0) to the `after` value (at
1) when both are numbers, else whichever side is a number (`after` first), else `undefined`.

### `isCodeStatisticsMeasure`

```ts
isCodeStatisticsMeasure(value: string): value is "blank" | "code" | "comment" | "files" | "lines"
```

Whether `value` is a `CodeStatisticsMeasure`, for validating a saved or declared option.

### `isCodeStatisticsScope`

```ts
isCodeStatisticsScope(value: unknown): value is "all" | "other" | "tests"
```

Whether `value` is a `CodeStatisticsScope`, for validating a saved or declared option.

### `isContainment`

```ts
isContainment(extraction: ContainmentSource): { (relationship: Relationship): false | true }
```

Whether a relationship of an extraction means containment (`from` contains `to`): `contains` in every schema, and the
containment its domain schema and vocabularies define (a database table's `constraint` and `index`; a
dependency-injection service's registrations and a registration's implementation, by their entity kinds).

### `isScopeChange`

```ts
isScopeChange(row: Pick<ScopeRow, "correspondence" | "status">): false | true
```

Whether a row is one of a comparison's changes: its status, or its identity (a rename, split or merge), changed.

### `kindWords`

```ts
kindWords(kind: string): Array<string>
```

A kind's words: camel case, kebab case and snake case split, capitalized words lowercased (`devDependencies` → `dev dependencies`).

### `matchesFilter`

```ts
matchesFilter(change: EntityChange<Entity | Relationship>, state: Pick<ViewerState, "kind" | "search" | "status">): false | true
```

Whether a row passes the viewer's filters: its `status` equals `state.status` (unless `all`), either version has
`state.kind` (unless empty), and either version's ID, label, kind or JSON `data` contains the trimmed `state.search`,
ignoring case (an empty search matches).

### `motionWindow`

```ts
motionWindow(step: Pick<ScheduledStep, "radius" | "time"> & Partial<Pick<ScheduledStep, "lead" | "tail" | "travel">>): { "radius": number; "time": number }
```

The part of a step's window in which things move: all of it, less its
reading lead and tail.

### `openingFloorPx`

```ts
openingFloorPx: 8
```

The smallest text, in CSS px, a zoomable canvas (a scroll container marked
`data-zoom`) opens with. It opens fitted, everything in view, unless that
draws its smallest text below this: then it opens zoomed until that text is
this size, at the content's start (its top left, or the top centre of a
centred layout), and the person scrolls and pans the rest; a diff, or a host's
focus (`RendererFocus`), opens on its changes instead. Fit to view still
shows everything, however small. The kit's `useStageZoom` applies it and the
built-in `opens-fitted` check verifies it. Added on 2026-11-10, the day
always fitting was adopted, after fitting drew the largest graphs' text at
2-6 px.

### `phaseProgress`

```ts
phaseProgress(local: number, phase: readonly [number, number]): number
```

Progress through one phase of a step (see `stepPhases`), eased.

### `pluralWord`

```ts
pluralWord(word: string): string
```

A word's English plural, by the simple rules: `class` → `classes`, `policy` → `policies`, `key` → `keys`.

### `presence`

```ts
presence(change: EntityChange<Entity | Relationship>, local: number): number
```

Visibility of an item at `local`, its progress through its own comparison
step's motion (`stepProgress`, which waits out the step's reading lead): a
removal fades out in the first phase and an addition fades in in the last
(`stepPhases`).

### `Presentation`

```ts
type Presentation = "domain" | "graph" | "table"
```

Which view a renderer that offers several shows: its own domain view, a generic graph or a table.

### `PresentationFrame`

```ts
interface PresentationFrame
```

Every visible item at one progress, as `createFrame` presents it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `edges` | `"edges": Array<PresentedEdge>` | The visible relationships, in row ID order, each never more opaque than its endpoints. |
| `emphasis` | `"emphasis": number` | The host-style change emphasis at `progress` (`diffEmphasis`): 0 at both endpoints and for an extraction. |
| `nodes` | `"nodes": Array<Presented<Entity>>` | The visible entities, in row ID order. |
| `progress` | `"progress": number` | The host's progress. |
| `schedule` | `"schedule": Array<ScheduledStep>` | The steps on the progress axis this frame was timed by (empty for an extraction). |
| `staged` | `"staged": number` | The staged clock: the share of the comparison's steps whose motion phase (`stepPhases.move`) has completed. It only moves inside step windows. Use it for motion shared by many items (a whole layout); time individual items by their `local` progress. |

### `presentComparison`

```ts
presentComparison(before: Extraction, after: Extraction, comparison: Comparison): PresentedChanges
```

Pairs the before and after items of a comparator-produced comparison. Items a
comparison does not mention are unchanged under their own ID. Identity comes
exclusively from the comparison; nothing is inferred here.

### `Presented`

```ts
interface Presented<T>
```

One item of a `PresentationFrame`: the version to draw now and how strongly.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `"change": EntityChange<T>` | The item's row, with both versions and its status. |
| `emphasis` | `"emphasis": number` | Change emphasis from 0 to 1: the frame's `emphasis` scaled by `rise`; 0 for an unchanged, unrenamed item. |
| `entity` | `"entity": T` | The version to draw: `before` until halfway through the item's step, then `after` (whichever exists). |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The item's row ID (`EntityChange.id`), stable across the transition. |
| `local` | `"local": number` | Progress through this item's own comparison step: 0 before it, 1 after it; 0 for an item no step changes, 1 in an extraction. |
| `opacity` | `"opacity": number` | Visibility from 0 to 1 (`presence`); items at 0 are left out of the frame. |
| `rise` | `"rise": number` | Share of the change highlighting this item shows now (`emphasisRise`): 0 before its step begins. |

### `PresentedChanges`

```ts
interface PresentedChanges extends Partial<PresentedOrder>
```

Comparison changes expanded into per-item before/after pairs for
presentation, with the comparison's steps resolved to those rows (absent
only when a caller builds the pairs by hand).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `entities` | `"entities": Array<EntityChange<Entity>>` | One row per entity, in ID order. |
| `relationships` | `"relationships": Array<EntityChange<Relationship>>` | One row per relationship, in ID order. |
| `reverse` | `"reverse"?: "explicit" \| "mirror"` | How playing backward orders steps: the forward steps reversed, or `reverseSteps`. |
| `reverseSteps` | `"reverseSteps"?: Array<PresentedStep>` | Backward presentation order (first presented when leaving progress 1) when `reverse` is `explicit`. |
| `steps` | `"steps"?: Array<PresentedStep>` | Steps in forward presentation order. |

### `PresentedEdge`

```ts
interface PresentedEdge extends Presented<Relationship>
```

A relationship of a `PresentationFrame`, with its endpoints resolved to the frame's entity rows.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `"change": EntityChange<Relationship>` | The item's row, with both versions and its status. |
| `emphasis` | `"emphasis": number` | Change emphasis from 0 to 1: the frame's `emphasis` scaled by `rise`; 0 for an unchanged, unrenamed item. |
| `entity` | `"entity": Relationship` | The version to draw: `before` until halfway through the item's step, then `after` (whichever exists). |
| `from` | `"from": string` | The source entity's row ID (`Presented.id`), which may differ from `entity.from` after a rename. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The item's row ID (`EntityChange.id`), stable across the transition. |
| `local` | `"local": number` | Progress through this item's own comparison step: 0 before it, 1 after it; 0 for an item no step changes, 1 in an extraction. |
| `opacity` | `"opacity": number` | Visibility from 0 to 1 (`presence`); items at 0 are left out of the frame. |
| `rise` | `"rise": number` | Share of the change highlighting this item shows now (`emphasisRise`): 0 before its step begins. |
| `to` | `"to": string` | The target entity's row ID (`Presented.id`), which may differ from `entity.to` after a rename. |

### `PresentedOrder`

```ts
interface PresentedOrder
```

The comparison's presentation order in presented-row space.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `reverse` | `"reverse": "explicit" \| "mirror"` | How playing backward orders steps: the forward steps reversed, or `reverseSteps`. |
| `reverseSteps` | `"reverseSteps"?: Array<PresentedStep>` | Backward presentation order (first presented when leaving progress 1) when `reverse` is `explicit`. |
| `steps` | `"steps": Array<PresentedStep>` | Steps in forward presentation order. |

### `PresentedStep`

```ts
interface PresentedStep
```

One comparison step in presented-row space. `kind` is inferred from the
entity members' statuses (all removed: `remove`, all added: `add`,
otherwise `restructure`; a step with no entities keeps its declared kind),
so a step without a declared kind, or with a kind that contradicts its
members, still animates coherently. `declaredKind` keeps the comparator's
own label.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `adds` | `"adds"?: false \| true` | Whether the step adds an entity or relationship (absent: whether `kind` is `add`). |
| `declaredKind` | `"declaredKind"?: "add" \| "remove" \| "restructure"` | The kind the comparator declared, when it declared one. |
| `entities` | `"entities": Array<string>` | Presented entity row IDs that change in this step. |
| `index` | `"index": number` | The step's position in its order, from 0; a final step for unplaced changes comes last. |
| `kind` | `"kind": "add" \| "remove" \| "restructure"` | The kind the step animates as, inferred from its entity rows. |
| `relationships` | `"relationships": Array<string>` | Presented relationship row IDs that change in this step. |
| `removes` | `"removes"?: false \| true` | Whether the step removes an entity or relationship (absent: whether `kind` is `remove`). |
| `summary` | `"summary"?: string` | The comparator's one-line description of the step, for captions; absent when it gave none. |

### `presentOrder`

```ts
presentOrder(rows: { "entities": Array<{ "after"?: undefined | { "id": string }; "before"?: undefined | { "id": string }; "id": string; "status": string }>; "relationships": Array<{ "after"?: undefined | { "id": string }; "before"?: undefined | { "id": string }; "id": string; "status": string }> }, comparison: Comparison): PresentedOrder
```

Resolves a comparison's steps (and explicit `reverseSteps`) from change IDs
to the presented rows that show them, including further split parts and
merged sources. A validated comparison places every change; anything left
over still animates, in a final step.

### `Quantity`

```ts
interface Quantity
```

A measured value with its unit.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `unit` | `"unit": string` | An exact label such as `ms` or `lines of code`, compared as text and never converted; empty when unknown. |
| `value` | `"value": number \| undefined` | The finite measurement, or `undefined` when it is missing, which is not the same as zero. |

### `quantityAt`

```ts
quantityAt(change: EntityChange<Entity>, progress: number, key?: string, unit?: string | undefined): Quantity
```

Units are exact labels, not conversion instructions. Missing measurements are not zero.

### `QuantityDomain`

```ts
interface QuantityDomain
```

The range a scale covers for one unit, always including zero (`quantityDomains`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `max` | `"max": number` | The largest value, at least 0. |
| `min` | `"min": number` | The smallest value, at most 0. |

### `quantityDomains`

```ts
quantityDomains(quantities: Iterable<Quantity, any, any>): Map<string, QuantityDomain>
```

One zero-anchored domain per unit, computed from both unfiltered endpoints.

### `quantityGeometry`

```ts
quantityGeometry(value: number | undefined, domain: QuantityDomain): QuantityGeometry
```

Lays `value` out on a track for `domain`, scaled so the domain's largest magnitude spans it: zero-anchored, so
negative values extend left of `zero` and positive ones right. A missing value, or an all-zero domain, has no width.

### `QuantityGeometry`

```ts
interface QuantityGeometry
```

Where a bar sits on a zero-anchored track, as fractions of the track's length from its start (0 to 1).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `left` | `"left": number` | Where the bar starts: at `zero` for a positive value, at the value for a negative one. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The bar's length, never negative; 0 for a missing value. |
| `zero` | `"zero": number` | Where zero is: 0 for a domain without negatives, further in when it has some. |

### `quantityShares`

```ts
quantityShares(values: Array<number | undefined>): Array<number> | undefined
```

Each value's share of their total, summing to 1, for share charts; all zeros when every value is 0. `undefined`
when any value is missing, negative or not finite, since a share of an unknown or negative total means nothing.

### `readingShare`

```ts
readingShare: 1
```

The reading policy: how long, in step slots, a step that takes something
away keeps still to show it before it leaves. The step's emphasis rises over
the first fifth of its reading part and holds while nothing moves, so what
is about to disappear is readable (about a second at 1× speed with the host's
default pace, `timelineSlots`) before it fades and its gap closes. The other
changes need no reading part: an arrival fades in already emphasized and
stays so through the hold after its step until the host's endpoint fade, and
a change that stays is emphasized as it changes. This is the one place
reading time is decided; renderers never add their own.

### `regenerated`

```ts
regenerated(change: { "status"?: string | undefined; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }): false | true
```

Whether a change only regenerated generated values from the same inputs: `unchanged`, with a generated `varied`
entry. Like any variation within tolerance it is presented as unchanged; hosts count it as "regenerated".

### `relationshipLabel`

```ts
relationshipLabel(relationship: Pick<Relationship, "from" | "kind" | "label" | "to">, entityLabel?: undefined | { (id: string): string | undefined }): string
```

A readable name for a relationship: its own `label` when it has one, else
its endpoints' labels joined by an arrow, with the kind when it says
something, for example "api → queue (publishes)". `entityLabel` looks up an
entity's label in the extraction the relationship comes from; endpoints it
doesn't know show their IDs.

### `RowContext`

```ts
interface RowContext
```

A change row's context: the rows that give it context, and the comparator rules that added any.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `derived` | `"derived": false \| true` | Whether it was derived from the comparison's structure because the comparison carries no context at all (one saved before comparisons had context). |
| `rows` | `"rows": Array<string>` | The row IDs of its context, in the order found. |
| `rules` | `"rules": Array<string>` | The comparator `context` rules that added to it (`ChangeContext.rules`). |

### `rowContexts`

```ts
rowContexts(rows: Array<ScopeRow>, revisions: { "after": ContainmentSource; "before": ContainmentSource }): { (row: ScopeRow): RowContext }
```

The context of each change row of a comparison: the comparison's own (`Change.context`), none for a row it gives
none, or, for a comparison saved without any context, the structural derivation the Engine's core context makes (a
changed relationship's endpoints, and the items containing a changed or context entity, `isContainment`, with the
containment relationships between them). Returns a function from a row to its context.

### `ScheduledStep`

```ts
interface ScheduledStep extends PresentedStep
```

A step placed on the progress axis. The step changes only inside its window
`[time - radius, time + radius]`; windows never overlap, and consecutive
windows are separated by a hold of length `hold` in which nothing moves. A
step that takes something away in its direction of travel reads it first
(see `readingShare`): a still part of its window, its `lead` forward or its
`tail` for explicit reverse steps played backward, in which what is about
to leave is emphasized and read before it goes.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `adds` | `"adds"?: false \| true` | Whether the step adds an entity or relationship (absent: whether `kind` is `add`). |
| `declaredKind` | `"declaredKind"?: "add" \| "remove" \| "restructure"` | The kind the comparator declared, when it declared one. |
| `entities` | `"entities": Array<string>` | Presented entity row IDs that change in this step. |
| `hold` | `"hold": number` | Length of the still interval between this window and a neighbouring one. |
| `index` | `"index": number` | The step's position in its order, from 0; a final step for unplaced changes comes last. |
| `kind` | `"kind": "add" \| "remove" \| "restructure"` | The kind the step animates as, inferred from its entity rows. |
| `lead` | `"lead"?: number` | Length of the still part at the start of the step's window (lowest progress) in which what it removes is emphasized and read before it fades. 0 or absent for a step that removes nothing, and travelling backward. |
| `radius` | `"radius": number` | Half-width of the step's window, its reading lead and tail included. |
| `relationships` | `"relationships": Array<string>` | Presented relationship row IDs that change in this step. |
| `removes` | `"removes"?: false \| true` | Whether the step removes an entity or relationship (absent: whether `kind` is `remove`). |
| `summary` | `"summary"?: string` | The comparator's one-line description of the step, for captions; absent when it gave none. |
| `tail` | `"tail"?: number` | Length of the still part at the end of the step's window (highest progress): an explicit reverse step played backward reads what it takes away (the forward additions) there. 0 or absent otherwise. |
| `time` | `"time": number` | Centre of the step's window, in [0, 1]. |
| `travel` | `"travel": -1 \| 1` | The direction this schedule is travelled in: 1 forward (and for `mirror` order either way), -1 for `explicit` `reverseSteps` played backward. |

### `scheduleSteps`

```ts
scheduleSteps<S extends PresentedStep = PresentedStep>(order: { "reverse": "explicit" | "mirror"; "reverseSteps"?: Array<S> | undefined; "steps": Array<S> }, direction?: -1 | 1): Array<S & { "hold": number; "lead": number; "radius": number; "tail": number; "time": number; "travel": -1 | 1 }>
```

The steps placed on the progress axis, in ascending time. Playing forward,
or with `mirror` reverse order, uses the forward steps; playing backward
with `explicit` reverse order places `reverseSteps` so that the first one
happens first when leaving progress 1. Both schedules agree at the
endpoints, where every step has either not started or finished. A step that
removes something gets a reading lead; travelling backward through explicit
reverse steps, one that adds something gets a reading tail, the part that
backward travel enters first. Use a `DirectionLatch` to choose `direction`.

### `ScopeRow`

```ts
interface ScopeRow
```

A row as `changeContext` reads it: a host row, or a presented change (`scopeRows`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after": Array<string>` | The row's item IDs in the after extraction. |
| `before` | `"before": Array<string>` | The row's item IDs in the before extraction. |
| `collection` | `"collection": "entities" \| "relationships"` | Whether the row is an entity or a relationship. |
| `context` | `"context"?: ChangeContext \| undefined` | The comparison's context for the change (`Change.context`); absent for a comparison saved without it. |
| `correspondence` | `"correspondence"?: "declared" \| "exact" \| "merge" \| "none" \| "split" \| undefined` | How the comparison matched the row's items; anything but `exact` is an identity change. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The row's ID: the change's ID, or the item's own for an unchanged one. |
| `status` | `"status"?: "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "unchanged" \| undefined` | The comparison's status for the row; `unchanged` (or absent) for an item it doesn't mention. |

### `scopeRows`

```ts
scopeRows(presented: Pick<PresentedChanges, "entities" | "relationships">): Array<ScopeRow>
```

A presented comparison's rows (`presentComparison`) as `changeContext` reads them.

### `sentenceCase`

```ts
sentenceCase(text: string): string
```

Text as it starts a sentence or a label: its first letter capitalized (`data source` → `Data source`), unless its
first word is a name written in lowercase (`npm package` stays `npm package`; see `lowercaseNames`).

### `sharedUnit`

```ts
sharedUnit(entities: Iterable<Entity | undefined, any, any>): string | undefined
```

The unit every one of these entities' measurements shares (`data.unit`), or undefined when they differ or have none.

### `snapshotChanges`

```ts
snapshotChanges<T extends { "id": string }>(entities: Array<T>): Array<EntityChange<T>>
```

Rows for a single extraction's items: each `unchanged`, with only `after`, under its own ID, in the given order.

### `statisticsCount`

```ts
statisticsCount(entity: Entity | undefined, key: "blank" | "code" | "comment" | "files" | "lines" | "value", scope?: "all" | "other" | "tests"): number | undefined
```

A language's count of `key` within `scope`. Test counts (`testFiles`,
`testCode`, `testComment`, `testBlank`, `testLines`) are a subset of the
totals, so `other` is the total minus the test count. Undefined when the
extraction has no such measurement.

### `StatisticsKey`

```ts
type StatisticsKey = "blank" | "code" | "comment" | "files" | "lines" | "value"
```

What a statistics row counts: a code-statistics measure, or a generic metric's `data.value` (see `hasCodeCounts`).

### `StatisticsRow`

```ts
interface StatisticsRow extends Quantity
```

One bar of a statistics chart, at the frame's progress (`statisticsRows`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `"id": string` | The language's row ID; without `byLanguage`, `composition:code`, `composition:comment` or `composition:blank`. |
| `label` | `"label": string` | The language's label (else its ID), or `Code`, `Comments` or `Blank`. |
| `node` | `"node"?: Presented<Entity>` | The language's frame node; absent for composition rows. |
| `opacity` | `"opacity": number` | The language's presence from its frame node; 1 for composition rows. |
| `unit` | `"unit": string` | An exact label such as `ms` or `lines of code`, compared as text and never converted; empty when unknown. |
| `value` | `"value": number \| undefined` | The finite measurement, or `undefined` when it is missing, which is not the same as zero. |

### `statisticsRows`

```ts
statisticsRows(frame: PresentationFrame, options: CodeStatisticsOptions): Array<StatisticsRow>
```

Aggregates collected counts for presentation, each language at its own step (`local`) and in `options.scope`; never invents entity correspondence or change status.

### `stepEnds`

```ts
stepEnds(schedule: Array<Pick<ScheduledStep, "hold" | "radius" | "time">>, direction?: -1 | 1): Array<number>
```

Progress values where a host may hold between steps: for each step, the
middle of the hold that follows it in the direction of travel (forward,
after its window; backward, before it), so seeking there always shows a
settled frame. Endpoints are omitted because hosts always stop there.
Report them with `client.steps`.

### `stepHolds`

```ts
stepHolds(schedule: Array<Pick<ScheduledStep, "radius" | "time">>): Array<{ "end": number; "start": number }>
```

The still intervals of a schedule, in ascending order: before the first
window, between consecutive windows and after the last. Nothing driven by
the schedule moves inside them.

### `stepHoldShare`

```ts
stepHoldShare: number
```

The hold policy: the share of every step's slot in which nothing moves. Host
playback is continuous, so a still interval between consecutive windows is
what makes shapes visibly settle at each step while progress keeps moving.
The headroom before the first and after the last step is at least as long.
This is the one place step holds are decided; renderers never add their own.

### `StepKind`

```ts
type StepKind = "add" | "remove" | "restructure"
```

What a step does, which decides its choreography (`stepWindows` in the kit): `remove` fades items out, then closes
the gap; `add` makes room, then fades items in; `restructure` moves and rewires what stays.

### `stepPhases`

```ts
stepPhases: { "fadeIn": readonly [0.7, 1]; "fadeOut": readonly [0, 0.3]; "move": readonly [0.3, 0.7] }
```

How a step uses its motion (`stepProgress`, after any reading lead), as
fractions of the step's own progress: leaving items fade out first, shared
motion (layouts, values, rewiring) happens in the middle, and arriving items
fade in last, so nothing that is about to leave or has just arrived is ever
caught mid-motion.

### `stepProgress`

```ts
stepProgress(step: Pick<ScheduledStep, "radius" | "time"> & Partial<Pick<ScheduledStep, "lead" | "tail" | "travel">>, progress: number): number
```

Progress through a step's motion (`motionWindow`): 0 until it starts moving,
after any reading lead, and 1 once it stops, before any reading tail, so it
is constant in every hold and while reading. Measured from the centre, so
the middle of the motion is exactly one half. Ease it for motion.

### `SummaryCount`

```ts
interface SummaryCount
```

The counts of one extraction kind in one collection: its total (in `after` for a comparison) and, for a comparison, its changes by status.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `added` | `"added"?: number` | For a comparison, added items of the kind (by their `after` item). |
| `collection` | `"collection": "entities" \| "relationships"` | Whether `kind` names entities or relationships. |
| `count` | `"count": number` | Items of the kind in the extraction, or in `after` for a comparison. |
| `kind` | `"kind": string` | The extraction kind, as the extraction spells it. |
| `modified` | `"modified"?: number` | For a comparison, modified items of the kind (by their `after` item). |
| `removed` | `"removed"?: number` | For a comparison, removed items of the kind (by their `before` item). |

### `summaryCounts`

```ts
summaryCounts(subject: { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "mode": "comparison" } | { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" }): Array<SummaryCount>
```

Counts each extraction kind of a subject, per collection: its items in the extraction, or in `after` for a
comparison, and for a comparison its changes by status (an added or modified change by its `after` item's kind, a
removed one by its `before` item's). Kinds come in the order a summary shows them by default: entity kinds, then
relationship kinds, each by count (largest first), then name. A kind only `before` has is counted with a total of 0.

### `summaryCountText`

```ts
summaryCountText(count: number, noun: SummaryNoun, locale?: string | undefined): string
```

A figure's total in words, in the locale's digits: `1 workspace`, `12 workspaces`.

### `SummaryDelta`

```ts
type SummaryDelta = "added" | "modified" | "removed"
```

One of `summaryDeltas`.

### `summaryDeltas`

```ts
summaryDeltas: readonly ["added", "removed", "modified"]
```

The change statuses a summary counts per kind.

### `summaryDeltaText`

```ts
summaryDeltaText(delta: "added" | "modified" | "removed", count: number, locale?: string | undefined): string
```

A change count as a summary bar shows it: `+2` added, `−1` removed (a minus sign), `~3` modified.

### `summaryDeltaWords`

```ts
summaryDeltaWords(delta: "added" | "modified" | "removed", count: number, locale?: string | undefined): string
```

A change count in words, for accessible names: `2 added`, `1 removed`, `3 modified`.

### `summaryItems`

```ts
summaryItems(subject: { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "mode": "comparison" } | { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" }, nouns?: undefined | { (kind: string, collection: "entities" | "relationships"): SummaryNoun | false | undefined } | { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun | false }): Array<SummaryCountItem>
```

A subject's summary, as a renderer posts it: a count figure (`type: 'count'`) per kind and collection (`summaryCounts`), worded with `nouns` where it gives
a noun and the host's words (`humanizeKind`) otherwise, leaving out the kinds it maps to `false`. The kinds an
object of nouns lists come first, in its order. At most `rendererLimits.summaryItems` figures.

### `SummaryNouns`

```ts
type SummaryNouns = { (kind: string, collection: "entities" | "relationships"): SummaryNoun | false | undefined } | { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun | false }
```

A renderer's words for kinds: a noun per kind, or `false` to leave a kind out of the summary. A key may name one
collection's kind (`relationships:index`), which wins over the bare kind. As an object, the kinds it lists come
first, in its order; as a function (given the kind and its collection), `undefined` keeps the host's words.

### `summarySentence`

```ts
summarySentence(items: Array<{ "added"?: number | undefined; "count": number; "modified"?: number | undefined; "noun": SummaryNoun; "removed"?: number | undefined }>, locale?: string | undefined): string
```

The summary as one sentence, the same words the summary bar shows: `12 workspaces · 18 dependencies` for one
revision, `12 workspaces +1 −1 · 18 dependencies +2` for a comparison (changes that didn't happen are left out).

### `SummarySubject`

```ts
type SummarySubject = { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "mode": "comparison" } | { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" }
```

What a summary counts: one extraction, or a comparison of two (the shape of `InitPayload` and the host's subject).

### `sumQuantities`

```ts
sumQuantities(values: Array<number | undefined>): number | undefined
```

The total of `values`, or `undefined` when any is missing or the sum isn't finite: a partial total would mislead.

### `timelineSlots`

```ts
timelineSlots(schedule: Array<Pick<ScheduledStep, "hold" | "lead" | "tail">>): number
```

How many step slots a schedule spans: one per step, plus its reading parts.
Report it with the step ends (`client.steps(ends, slots)`) so the host's
default pace gives every slot the same time, and reading never speeds up
the motion around it.

### `unit`

```ts
unit(value: number): number
```

`value` clamped to the unit interval, 0 to 1: the normal form of every progress the presentation helpers take.

### `variedBeyond`

```ts
variedBeyond(change: VariedChange): false | true
```

Whether a change is `modified` with a volatile value beyond its tolerance,
which presentations mark with the neutral `varied` icon beside the
change's status. A generated value regenerated from a changed basis isn't
one: it changed for a reason, which its field says (`generatedWords`).

### `variedBeyondLabel`

```ts
variedBeyondLabel: "Volatile field changed beyond tolerance"
```

The accessible name of the volatile marker (`variedBeyond`).

### `VariedChange`

```ts
interface VariedChange
```

A row with the comparison's status and volatile values (`EntityChange`, a host row).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `"status"?: "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "unchanged" \| undefined` | The row's change status; `variedWithin` looks for `unchanged` and `variedBeyond` for `modified`. |
| `varied` | `"varied"?: Array<Varied> \| undefined` | The comparison's volatile values for the row (`change.varied`), each within or beyond its tolerance. |

### `variedName`

```ts
variedName(path: string): string
```

A varied value's name for display: its pointer below `/data/`, segments
unescaped and joined with `/` (`/data/durationMs` is `durationMs`).

### `variedValue`

```ts
variedValue(item: unknown, path: string): unknown
```

The value a varied path (an RFC 6901 pointer into the item) points to, or `undefined`.

### `variedWithin`

```ts
variedWithin(change: VariedChange): false | true
```

Whether a change varied only within tolerance: `unchanged`, with `varied`.
Such an item is presented exactly as an unchanged one: no emphasis, status
or motion.

### `variedWithinTolerance`

```ts
variedWithinTolerance(change: { "status"?: string | undefined; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }): false | true
```

Whether a change is `unchanged` with a volatile value other than a generated one varied within its tolerance,
such as a duration: what hosts count as "varied within tolerance".

### `variedWords`

```ts
variedWords(within: false | true): string
```

How a varied value relates to its tolerance, in words: `within tolerance` or `beyond tolerance (volatile)`.

### `ViewerAction`

```ts
type ViewerAction = { "direction": -1 | 1; "type": "play" } | { "durationMs": number; "elapsedMs": number; "type": "advance" } | { "id": null | string; "type": "select" } | { "id": string; "type": "collapse" } | { "progress"?: number; "type": "reset" } | { "type": "kind"; "value": string } | { "type": "pause" } | { "type": "presentation"; "value": "domain" | "graph" | "table" } | { "type": "search"; "value": string } | { "type": "seek"; "value": number } | { "type": "statistics"; "value": Partial<CodeStatisticsOptions> } | { "type": "status"; "value": "added" | "all" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged" }
```

A change to `ViewerState`. `search`, `kind`, `status`, `presentation` and `select` set their field; `statistics`
merges options; `collapse` toggles an ID; `seek` jumps to a progress and pauses; `play` starts in a direction
(from the far end when already at the end it plays toward); `pause` stops; `advance` moves playback by `elapsedMs`
of a `durationMs`-long transition; `reset` returns to `initialViewerState(progress)`.

### `viewerReducer`

```ts
viewerReducer(state: ViewerState, action: { "direction": -1 | 1; "type": "play" } | { "durationMs": number; "elapsedMs": number; "type": "advance" } | { "id": null | string; "type": "select" } | { "id": string; "type": "collapse" } | { "progress"?: number; "type": "reset" } | { "type": "kind"; "value": string } | { "type": "pause" } | { "type": "presentation"; "value": "domain" | "graph" | "table" } | { "type": "search"; "value": string } | { "type": "seek"; "value": number } | { "type": "statistics"; "value": Partial<CodeStatisticsOptions> } | { "type": "status"; "value": "added" | "all" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged" }): ViewerState
```

Applies `action` to `state` without mutating it, for `useReducer`. Progress is clamped to 0 to 1; `advance` is a
no-op while paused and pauses on reaching the end it plays toward.

### `ViewerState`

```ts
interface ViewerState
```

A renderer's local viewing state, as `viewerReducer` keeps it: the search and filters `filterFrame` applies, the
chosen view, local playback, selection, collapsed groups and code-statistics options. Nothing here reaches the host.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `collapsed` | `"collapsed": ReadonlySet<string>` | IDs of collapsed items, whose descendants `visibleHierarchy` hides. |
| `direction` | `"direction": -1 \| 1` | The direction local playback runs: `1` toward after, `-1` toward before. |
| `kind` | `"kind": string` | The extraction kind to show, or an empty string for every kind. |
| `playing` | `"playing": false \| true` | Whether local playback is running; `advance` stops it at the end it plays toward. |
| `presentation` | `"presentation": "domain" \| "graph" \| "table"` | The view shown. |
| `progress` | `"progress": number` | Local presentation progress, from 0 (before) to 1 (after). |
| `search` | `"search": string` | Free-text search, matched case-insensitively (`matchesFilter`); empty matches everything. |
| `selectedId` | `"selectedId": null \| string` | The selected item's ID, or `null`. |
| `statistics` | `"statistics": CodeStatisticsOptions` | How code statistics are measured and charted. |
| `status` | `"status": "added" \| "all" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "unchanged"` | The change status to show, or `all`. |

### `ViewScope`

```ts
type ViewScope = "all" | "changes" | "noise"
```

The scopes of a comparison view: every item, the changes and their context, or the noise (items that only varied).

### `viewScopes`

```ts
viewScopes: Array<"all" | "changes" | "noise">
```

Every `ViewScope`, in the order a host offers them.

### `visibleHierarchy`

```ts
visibleHierarchy(frame: PresentationFrame, collapsed: ReadonlySet<string>): Set<string>
```

The IDs of `frame.nodes` still shown when the items in `collapsed` are collapsed: every node except the descendants
of a collapsed one, following edges from `from` to `to` (cycles are safe). Collapsed nodes themselves stay visible.

### `wordDiff`

```ts
wordDiff(before: string, after: string): Array<WordRun> | undefined
```

A word diff of two passages, as runs in reading order (removed text before the text that replaced it), or
`undefined` when either is too long to compare. Words, spaces and punctuation are the tokens.

### `WordRun`

```ts
interface WordRun
```

One run of a word diff: text both passages share, or text only one has.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `op` | `"op": "added" \| "removed" \| "same"` | `same` for text both passages have, `removed` for text only `before` has, `added` for text only `after` has. |
